title: VEL-WEEKENDER-LIVEOUT-02 v5 — flap mechanism fix
summary: SHIPPED 2026-08-24. VEL-WEEKENDER-GS-LIVEOUT-02-v5.mp4, 1080x1920, 35.69s, -14.9 LUFS. Two beats in v4 did not show the Weekender's real opening mechanism. The 14.0s beat is now REAL filmed footage of the actual bag opening. The 20.2s beat is a regenerated and re-animated S7 with the flap in frame. VO, caption cards and all twelve other beats are byte-identical to v4.

timelines.label: BEAT 1 — 14.0s 'so it keeps its shape'
timelines.source: was askme-ELEANOR-S11 library clip, now real 4K iPhone footage

beats.script: so it keeps its shape packed full or half empty
beats.note: Three tabs merged into one straight edge. No gold oval plate on the flap. The plate is on the BODY BAND instead, the exact inverse of the real bag. Interior reads cream canvas, not caramel leather.

beats.script: so it keeps its shape packed full or half empty
beats.visual: real hand folding the real flap all the way back
beats.note: Real footage of the actual bag. Opens on the closed flap with all three tabs and the gold oval keyhole plate, folds all the way back, ends on the caramel leather interior with the bag holding its shape. Nothing generated, so nothing to fail.

timelines.source: S7 regenerated on GPT Image 2 i2i, animated on Omni

beats.script: it just sat open by the bed for three days

beats.note: No flap, no handles, no staples, no turn post, no corner patches. Reads as a canvas basket with a leather rim. The animation pass then grew a drooping front handle that is not on the bag.

beats.note: Exact counts: three hanging tabs, one gold oval plate on the centre tab, two keyhole handle cutouts, two strap slots. Both handles anchored in the leather band. Correct knurled mushroom post. Both belt strap end plates above the corner patches.

beats.script: it just sat open by the bed for three days
beats.visual: she lifts the sweater out, bag still on the rug
beats.note: Every count holds through the whole move. Audited at three points across the clip plus the composed timeline frame with captions in place.

timelines.label: REJECTED — kept for the audit trail
timelines.source: 8 keyframes generated across two passes, 6 rejected

beats.visual: flap square to camera, most legible mechanism of the set
beats.note: Best flap in the set, but the motion pass carried two hardware defects from its keyframe: the knurled post rendered as a gold spiral, and both belt straps ran down onto the corner patches. Structural, so a FAIL, not an editor note.

beats.visual: first pass, same blocking as the pick
beats.note: Four strap slots on the flap instead of two, and the left belt strap ran onto the corner patch. Fixed in pass 2 by adding explicit counts to the prompt.
Flap counts correct but the rear handle is missing and the crop loses the silhouette.

notes.title: WHAT FIXED THE FLAP
notes.text: Two changes at once, after this geometry had failed about a dozen times across three runs. One, the i2i anchor moved off the closed hero and onto the real open-bag photographs. Two, the flap-tab language moved to the very front of the prompt written as a left-to-right reading of the flap edge, with explicit counts. Pass 1 without counts gave four slots on one candidate. Pass 2 with counts gave correct counts on every roll.

notes.title: WHY THE FIRST BEAT WENT TO REAL FOOTAGE
notes.text: Every engine merges the three tabs into one slab sooner or later. Real footage of the actual bag opening removes the failure mode entirely and is the strongest proof available for that VO line.

notes.title: PROCESS
notes.text: H was animated first and then thrown away over two hardware defects. That is the 8/24 law working as intended: a missing, invented or malformed structural element is a FAIL, never a note. Passing those as notes is what put the two defects into v4 in the first place.
